VOOL was founded by people from the electricity grid business who saw how much grid capacity goes unused.
We come from the grid business. That is why VOOL starts with the grid.
VOOL means “flow” or “current” in Estonian. We build EV charging that uses the electricity connection a building already has.

While working in the energy sector, the founders kept seeing the same thing: electricity connections sized for a peak that rarely comes, with most of the capacity unused. Ministry of Climate: legal obstacles to renovation (2026)
The recast Energy Performance of Buildings Directive, (EU) 2024/1275, Article 14, tells member states to make installing charging points simpler and faster, in particular in co-owners’ associations.
Member states must remove barriers such as needing the co-owners’ consent for a private charging point for the owner’s own use. A request can be refused only on serious and legitimate grounds.
Countries had until May 2026 to write this into national law, and they have done it in different ways. Check the rules in your country before the meeting.

What EU rules require for charging in new and renovated buildings, how to size the connection, and specification text for tenders.
Design charging into the building once, and size the connection smaller
New buildings must be prepared for charging. With load management at several fuse levels, the charging load fits a connection sized for the building.

The recast Energy Performance of Buildings Directive sets minimum requirements for new buildings and major renovations. Member states apply them through national law and may go further, so check the local rules.
New residential buildings with more than three parking spaces: pre-cabling for at least half of the spaces, ducting for the rest, and at least one charging point.
New non-residential buildings with more than five parking spaces: at least one charging point for every five spaces, pre-cabling for at least half and ducting for the rest.
Charging points must be capable of smart charging.
Chargers installed from 1 January 2027 must also support ISO 15118-20. See AFIR and ISO 15118.
